notes: A CORRECTION, NOT A NEW ADJUDICATION. bmdb 1551, pureftpd: API00-C rows labeled TP are re-derived under ADR-0011 (aurora-lint bbf240e9 caller-side checks, d9cb04d0 proof chains, 742a1571 libraries count as external). API00-C never flags a static function, so a closed caller set exists only for a non-static function linked solely into a plain executable. For pureftpd that is the pure-ftpd executables (libpureftpd.a is not installed): there is no -rdynamic, export list or dlopen of its own code. A row flips TP -> FP only when every call site (including every use of a wrapping macro, in every #ifdef arm) proves every flagged parameter non-null by a dominating explicit test, an address-of, an array or array offset, a literal, or a chain of caller parameters ending in one of those at every level. A prior dereference, assert/DEBUGASSERT, an untested field or global, or a test of a different expression is not proof. METHOD: a mechanical call-site pre-pass, then a first reader over every candidate, then a fresh-context refuter over every proposed flip. RESULT: 27 flip TP -> FP here, each reason naming its call sites. Refuted and left TP: src/bsd-glob.c:873 globfree, because the name also exists in libc, so the linker exports the executable definition and a loaded shared object (PAM/NSS module) can bind to it; that caller set is open. Key src/ftpd.c:3271 is not emitted by a current scan; the originally flagged parameters are shown non-null regardless. main() argv rows are left to bmdb 1548. Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. No precision claim is made here.
